diagnosis: Candidate/bad runs disproportionately repeat actions without gaining new state, especially repeated clicks, no-ops/waits, and scrolling.
expected_mechanism: A progress gate detects unchanged state and forces replanning, reducing unproductive loops and preserving steps for alternative approaches. Cost: state comparison and replanning add small latency and may interrupt rare cases where identical retries are necessary.
policy_text: Before repeating an action toward the same subgoal, compare the current observable state with the state before the previous attempt. If no relevant progress occurred, do not retry unchanged; diagnose the blocker and change the action, target, parameters, or plan. Permit one justified retry for transient failures.

quantitative_evidence.finding: Repeated operations have a net bad-minus-good excess of 1,261. Within this excess, repeated clicks contribute +639, no-ops +356, and scrolling +277; inspect, wait, and navigate strategies contribute +602, +356, and +306 respectively.
Base/good runs contain 224 repeated operations, so candidate runs show 6.63× as many and an excess of 1,261.
